label: rem:julia-set-reeb
title: Julia set of the Reeb flow on the exceptional divisor
html:
The q-deformed Reeb flow \phi_t^q (q-Reeb flow) restricted to the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) (Reeb on exceptional divisor) generates a discrete dynamical system. Its Julia set encodes the photon diffraction envelope.

The iteration. The substrate parameter q drives the main-cardioid parameterization of the Mandelbrot set:

  c(q) =  \tfrac{1}{2}e^{2\pi i q}
  - \tfrac{1}{4}e^{4\pi i q}.

The associated quadratic map f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) acts as the discrete-time skeleton of the continuous Reeb flow. Each iteration of f_q corresponds to one full circuit of the U(1) fiber above \mathcal{S}_c. The Julia set J(f_q) \subset \mathbb{C} marks the boundary between escaping orbits and bounded orbits. It is the fractal frontier of the Reeb dynamics.

Photon envelope. Photons propagate as exceptional-divisor flux, not as q-harmonic forms. Their diffraction envelope follows the Julia-set measure \mu_J (the natural invariant measure on J(f_q)), rather than the sinc{}^2 distribution of massive particles. The Hausdorff dimension d_H = d_H(q) of J(f_q) \cap S^1 governs the power-law tails of the photon envelope. It replaces the |\varTheta|^{-2} falloff of classical Airy diffraction with |\varTheta|^{-d_H}.

Julia set at the golden ratio. At the golden threshold q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2 \approx 0.382, the effective angle on the main cardioid is

  \varTheta_{\mathrm{gold}}
  =  2\pi/\varphi^2
   \approx  137.5°

This is the golden angle. It is the most irrational angle. Its continued fraction [0; 1, 1, 1, \ldots] converges slower than any other. At this rotation number, the Julia set J(f_{q_{\mathrm{gold}}}) develops a Siegel disk boundary. This yields the richest fractal structure among cardioid parameters. The golden rotation number is the hardest to linearize because the small denominators in the linearization series are maximally large.

Julia set at the reciprocal q_{\mathrm{gold}}^{-1} = \varphi^2. At the reciprocal, \varphi^2 = \varphi + 1. The effective angle is

  2\pi\varphi^2 \bmod 2\pi
  =  2\pi(\varphi^2 - 2)
  =  2\pi/\varphi
   \approx  222.5°,

which is the golden complement (360° - 137.5°). The cardioid parameterization is symmetric, so the Julia set at q = \varphi^2 has the same Hausdorff dimension as at q = 1/\varphi^2:

  d_H(\varphi^2) =  d_H(1/\varphi^2).

The asymmetry: Julia meets fiber. The Julia set is symmetric under q \leftrightarrow 1/q (via the complementary golden angle), but the elliptic fiber is not.

q = 1/\varphi^2 q = \varphi^2
Elliptic fiber \mathcal{E}_q Singular (node) Smooth (\Delta = -200, j = 160)
Julia set Siegel boundary, maximal d_H Same d_H (golden complement)
Reeb flow No smooth carrier Strong torsion, deep quantum
Physics No stable chiral structure Stable; Big Bang territory

At q = \varphi^2, the photon envelope exhibits its richest fractal structure (the same d_H as the golden threshold), and the Reeb bundle retains a smooth elliptic fiber. This characterizes the deep-quantum regime: maximal fractal diffraction paired with stable chiral geometry.

Information-theoretic content. The Hausdorff dimension d_H(q) measures the information density of the photon envelope. A higher d_H indicates that the diffraction pattern encodes more structure per unit angle. The golden angle maximizes d_H because the Fibonacci convergents of 1/\varphi are the worst rational approximants. The iteration f_q cannot lock into any periodic orbit. The dynamics must explore the full complexity of the Julia set. This directly connects to the golden-angle phyllotaxis of the Bring surface (golden ratio degeneration). The irrationality optimizing surface packing also maximizes the information content of photon scattering.

The experimental discriminant is the ratio of photon-to-electron envelope widths at identical slit geometries:

  \frac{w_{\mathrm{photon}}}{w_{\mathrm{electron}}}
  = 
  \frac{d_H}{2}
  \bigl(1 + (1 - q^{-1})^2
  \langle\Delta_\xi\rangle_e / \langle\Delta\rangle_e\bigr).

This ratio strictly depends on q, not on slit width or wavelength. It provides a sharp experimental test of the Julia-set envelope prediction.
